name: AlmanacA0a
build_class_reason: every shipped file matches its manifest hash
build_class_rule: ALMANAC_EDITION_MANIFEST §12.7: a distributable is PUBLISHABLE only with zero DRIFT rows. Any DRIFT means the zip would freeze bytes the tree has not frozen, so the build is a PREVIEW and declares itself one on its own face. The §12.2 cold re-hash at deposit is what turns a preview into a publishable build.
edition: AlmanacA0a — the centre of the even hybrid family quantum GL1 (PILOT)

counts.note: THREE DISTINCT NUMBERS DESCRIBE THIS ARTIFACT, each defined below, so the authoritative one is always explicit.
counts.files_shipped_means: every file in the EDITION except the two written last, CHECKSUMS.txt and DIST_MANIFEST.json, which cannot hash themselves. This is the number of lines in CHECKSUMS.txt.
counts.files_on_disk_means: files_shipped, plus CHECKSUMS.txt and DIST_MANIFEST.json, plus the 8 repository-furniture files at the archive root (.gitignore, .gitlab-ci.yml, .nojekyll, AGENTS.md, CITATION.cff, LICENSE, LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0, README.md), which ship but sit outside the edition CHECKSUMS.txt certifies. This is what `find . -type f` reports in the unzipped directory.
counts.provenance_rows_means: rows in files[] below: one per shipped file, edition and root furniture alike, so provenance_rows = files_shipped + 8 root files. (Before 2026-08-26 this was 69 against 80 shipped, because the Palomar layer, the front matter and the renderer were copied without being recorded. hypervisorA caught it at re-acceptance.)

file_count_means: alias of counts.files_shipped, kept for readers of earlier editions

integrity.how_to_read_this: DRIFT means the shipped bytes differ from the hash recorded in the edition manifest. The edition's rows are NOT frozen until deposit, so drift before that point is expected and governed — but it is recorded here rather than smoothed over, because a manifest hash that no longer matches its file is exactly the kind of green-looking wrong answer this project refuses to ship.

slice_rule.reproduce: the matching lines of Sandbox.lean, sorted, joined by newline, one trailing newline, sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes
slice_rule.why: A whole-file hash was the wrong instrument for this row's claim and was wrong in BOTH directions: it fired on an import added for the AN tree, which has nothing to do with GL1, and it would NOT have fired if a GL1 import were removed while the file changed size elsewhere. The slice isolates the bytes the claim is about, so it fires exactly when a GL1 source leaves the import root and at no other time.

files.shipped_is: a SLICE of the source file, not the file - the lines its regex selects, sorted. The rule ships with it so a reader reproduces it from their own copy of the source.
